abstract: A Lean 4 development of the classification of Barker sequences of odd length. A Barker sequence of length n is a sequence h of n signs whose aperiodic autocorrelations C(k), the sum over j < n - k of h(j) h(j + k), satisfy |C(k)| <= 1 for 0 < k < n. Turyn and Storer (1961) stated, and gave a proof, that a Barker sequence of odd length n > 1 has length 3, 5, 7, 11 or 13 (length 1 is admitted here: it has no nontrivial shift). Theorem 1(iv) of Turyn–Storer, on which their proof relies, is false as stated (Willms 2014, explicit counterexamples); per Schmidt–Willms (footnote 1) parts (ii) and (iii) imply (iv) on a corrected range that suffices for the induction, and independent proofs exist (Borwein–Erdélyi 2013; Schmidt–Willms 2016, the proof formalized here). The proof formalized is that of Schmidt and Willms (2016), recast so that the classification needs no enumeration of sequences: for odd n and m = (n - 1)/2, odd shifts have autocorrelation 0 and even shifts (-1)^m (from C(u) + C(n - u) = n mod 4); skew-symmetry h(k) h(n - 1 - k) = (-1)^(m + k); the folded identity, the sum over k <= w of (-1)^k h(k) h(w - k), equals 1 for every even w <= n - 3; the doubling law h(u - 1) h(u) = h(2u - 1) h(2u) for 1 <= u <= (n - 3)/2; Schmidt and Willms's Lemmas 3 and 4 in sign-change form (for n >= 7 and h(0) = h(1), with p the first sign change and q the first sign change not divisible by p, both are odd and 2q - 3 <= n <= p + q + 1, Lemma 4 by one generating-function identity for the folded sums); and an endgame that leaves n in {7, 11, 13}, excluding n = 9 by skew-symmetry and doubling, with the alternation h(j) -> (-1)^j h(j) for the normalization h(0) = h(1). Eight witnesses, one at each length 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11 and 13, are Barker by decide, and every Barker sequence of odd length equals a fixed sequence of its length (canon) up to negation and alternation, by a kernel enumeration of the 2^n sign patterns at each of the six odd lengths. Also proved: the even reduction of Turyn and Storer's footnote 2, that a Barker sequence of even length n > 2 has 4 | n and yields a real circulant Hadamard matrix of order n. Given the even-length classification as an explicit hypothesis (every Barker sequence of positive even length has length 2 or 4, the statement even_length_eq_two_or_four of openai/math, family 179), a Barker sequence of positive length n exists exactly when n is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11 or 13, and every Barker sequence has length at most 13; the same follows from the hypothesis that real circulant Hadamard matrices of positive order exist only at orders 1 and 4 (the forward direction of exists_iff_order_one_or_four of openai/math), through the even reduction. The seven definitions are restated from openai/math's two challenge files, character for character except the two Fin-bound proofs inside aperiodic (explicit terms in place of by omega, which under the module system yields module-private auxiliary theorems the comparator rejects), so its two theorems discharge the hypotheses, even_length_eq_two_or_four by unfolding alone and exists_iff_order_one_or_four by unfolding and Iff.mp; they are not proved here. The restated definitions and the adapted parts named in NOTICE derive from Apache-2.0 work of OpenAI (NOTICE, LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt); the rest is MIT.

related_formalizations.note: The Lean tree of openai/math (family 179): lean/ComparatorChallenges/EvenBarker.lean and CirculantHadamard.lean supply the seven restated definitions and the two statements behind the hypotheses (heven is the first, hcirc the forward direction of the second); lean/OAI/LinearAlgebra/Barker/ proves the even half (four_dvd_length, existsRealCirculantHadamard_of_even_barker, even_length_eq_two_or_four). This entry re-proves the first two in its own environment as four_dvd_of_even and existsRealCirculantHadamard_of_even (the definition periodic and two lemmas adapted, see NOTICE). It does not prove even_length_eq_two_or_four: the argument of that theorem appears here only with the hypothesis hcirc, the forward direction of the circulant Hadamard statement (exists_iff_of_circulantHadamard, length_le_thirteen_of_circulantHadamard). The odd half, the structure theorems and the uniqueness theorem are not formalized there. Lean v4.34.1, not registered on Palomar.

States the Barker conjecture (every Barker sequence has length at most 13, over List ℤ) as an open statement with a sorry; this entry proves its odd-length half in the Fin-indexed vocabulary of openai/math and the full statement under the even-length hypothesis. No code is shared.
